headline: Vantage deal closes, real estate keeps compounding
summary_short: Howard Hughes closed its ~$2.1 billion Vantage acquisition on June 4, 2026; net income attributable to common stockholders rose to $158.4 million (from a $12.1 million loss a year ago) as the real estate platform's MPC EBT grew 32% y/y to $134.7 million.
summary_long: Howard Hughes closed its ~$2.1 billion Vantage acquisition on June 4, 2026, partly funded by $1.0 billion of Series A preferred stock sold to Pershing Square. Vantage is consolidated only for the June 4-30 stub period ($97.2M premiums, $4.7M underwriting income, $20.8M pretax loss, 95% combined ratio); the company says resulting revenue, net income, and EPS comparisons to prior periods aren't comparable or run-rate. Real estate MPC EBT rose 32% y/y to $134.7M on strong land pricing; condo closings at The Park Ward Village (97% of units sold) drove a $706.3M jump in condominium revenue. Cash and equivalents reached $2,648.0M; stockholders' equity rose to $3,960.4M. No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Increase driven primarily by condominium unit closings at The Park Ward Village ($706.3M vs $0.2M prior year, 97% of units sold generating $226.6M net proceeds) plus Vantage's stub-period contribution of $97.2M premiums and $11.0M investment income; company states the comparison is not run-rate.

Swing to a $158.4M profit from a $12.1M prior-year loss reflects the same condo-closing revenue plus a $51.8M gain on real estate asset sales, partly offset by a $38.3M investment loss tied to the Vantage transaction; company flags the comparison as not run-rate.
Basic and diluted EPS were identical at $2.68 (vs -$0.22 a year ago), driven by the same net-income swing above; weighted diluted shares rose 6.9% y/y on shares tied to the Pershing Square financing.

Operating income rose to $239.6M from $67.9M largely because the Strategic Developments segment swung to $124.4M of operating income from a $4.5M loss as condo sales closed; MPC and Operating Assets segments also grew.
Company attributes the EBT increase to strong land pricing: 206.7 residential acres sold at a $1.2M/acre average and 9.8 commercial acres at a $0.9M/acre average during H1 2026.
Release states NOI "continued to grow" including contributions from unconsolidated ventures but gives no specific driver beyond the dollar increase itself; not otherwise explained.

Cash build to $2,648.0M reflects Vantage's consolidated cash balance plus proceeds from the $1.0B Pershing Square preferred stock issuance; company cites this as part of its "strong liquidity position."

Release frames the quarter around Vantage's June 4 close, reshaping HHH into two platforms, Howard Hughes Communities and Vantage; no earnings-call transcript was available at fetch time, only the press release.
